results.name: Persona-Story Alignment
results.reasoning: The generated document includes a migration/backward-compatibility story under Tenant User ('provide either the legacy ID or the name during the migration period') and frames the entire feature around ID-to-name migration support, while the gold standard explicitly scopes out backward compatibility; more critically, no misattribution of sanitization exists but the Cloud Infrastructure Admin story ('audit which resources are referenced') doesn't match the gold standard's infrastructure ops persona stories, and the generated document lacks the 'All Personas' category entirely, misrepresenting cross-cutting UI/CLI stories under wrong or absent personas.
quotes: As a Cloud Infrastructure Admin, I want to be able to audit which resources are referenced
As a Tenant User, I want to provide either the legacy ID or the name of a referenced resource during the migration period
No backward-compatible transition period — clean replacement

results.name: In Scope / Out of Scope Accuracy
results.reasoning: The generated document critically misrepresents scope: it includes a backward-compatible migration period (accepting legacy ID-based references) which the gold standard explicitly places Out of Scope, and omits gold's Out of Scope item 'Backward compatibility with the previous string-based reference format'. It also omits UI/CLI updates from In Scope (gold includes them), misses 'No backward-compatible transition period — clean replacement' as an In Scope item, and adds scope-creep items like cross-tenant audit and inconsistent-ID validation not in the gold.
quotes: No backward-compatible transition period — clean replacement of the current format
Backward compatibility with the previous string-based reference format
UI, CLI, and API all updated to support the new reference format

results.name: Problem Statement Quality
results.reasoning: The Problem Statement describes only user pain points (invalid references caught at provisioning time, unclear cross-tenant semantics, unmanageable migration) without describing the solution or how the feature works.
quotes: Invalid or mistyped references are only caught at provisioning time — not at submission — leading to failed operations
The API also cannot express whether a reference targets an object in the same tenant
reference fields cannot evolve without breaking every existing API consumer

results.reasoning: The generated document addresses async status visibility indirectly through submission-time validation and descriptive errors, but this feature is primarily synchronous validation, not async resource creation, so the criterion is adequately met.
